basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 25.' and it opens 'Vers. 25. Qui prior egressus fuerat, vocatus est Edom vel Rufus. Edom enim interpretatur'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 25. Qui prior egressus fuerat, vocatus est Edom vel Rufus. Edom enim interpretatur rufus vel rubeus, a quo Idumaei vocantur. Hispidus, id est setosus, quod Hebraice dicitur Seir a quo mons Seir vocatus est. Ergo novimus eum trinomium fuisse, quia vocatus est Esau, Edom, Seir. Jacob interpretatur supplantator. Mystice Jacob gentilem populum videlicet Judaicum supplantavit, id est sub planta misit, quia quasi super eum ascendit, quando ejus dignitatem accepit.
